# Best power station and solar combos for an RV

No single combo fits every rig. The right one depends on what you run, especially whether you need the roof A/C. Here are the picks by use case. The sources didn't give me direct retailer links for most of these, so I've linked the pages that list each product and its "check price" buttons. Confirm current prices there.

## Weekend or light use (fridge, lights, laptop, Starlink)
**EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** (1,024Wh, 1,800W, about 28 lb) is the top overall pick in one camping roundup. It accepts up to 1,000W of solar across two 500W inputs and expands to 5kWh. [Source](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)
- **Budget or lighter alternative:** The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (1,070Wh, about 23.8 lb) is simpler, but its solar input tops out at 400W. Two 200W SolarSaga panels would use all of it. It also isn't expandable. [Source](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)
- **Panels:** One guide suggests a Renogy 200W foldable solar suitcase for this class. [Source](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)

## Multi-day boondocking
**BLUETTI AC200L** (2,048Wh, 2,400W, 1,200W solar input, about 62 lb) is the value pick. A guide cites its built-in 30A RV outlet. [Source 1](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), [Source 2](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- Its high solar ceiling means you can add panels over time. A 300–400W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun. [Source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- **Alternative:** The Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 (2,042Wh) is lighter at about 39.5 lb, but it's capped at 400W of solar. [Source](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

## Running the roof A/C or full-time RVing
- **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** (4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous, 8,000W surge, expandable past 12kWh) is the best all-rounder in one RV comparison. It's heavy, so lifting it is a two-person job. [Source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro** (3,024Wh, 3,000W) is the simpler option for A/C. It can start a 13,500 BTU unit without a soft-start kit. [Source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- **ALLPOWERS R4000** (3,456Wh, 3,600W at 120V, 2,000W solar input, 5-year warranty) is a lower-cost large option. It's listed at $1,499, and the page cites codes such as EXTRA12 (expires Nov 15, 2026). It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it's not hand-portable. [Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) (affiliate link; the retailer pays a commission at no cost to you).

## Tips before you buy
- **Match panels to the solar input limit.** A big array on a unit with a low ceiling is wasted. The AC200P's 700W cap, for example, is lower than the AC200L's. [Source](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life)
- **Size for startup watts.** A 13,500 BTU A/C draws about 1,500W running and spikes past 3,000W on startup. [Source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- **Panels are usually sold separately.** Bundled panel wattage varies by package.
- **Get an electrician for hardwiring.** Don't wire anything permanently into the RV yourself.
- **Prices vary between sources.** Some reviews are affiliate-driven, so check current specs and prices at checkout.

If you tell me your RV type, whether you need A/C, and your budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
